mainTopic: The unsolved bargaining-vow question, רב אסי on the four vows, and the different ways sages opened a vow (פותחין בחרטה)
overview: The גמרא first shows that the cold-water case in the משנה cannot settle the question of a bargaining vow, so that question stays unresolved (תבעי). Next, רב יהודה quotes רב אסי: the four vows of the משנה still need a חכם. שמואל objects, because the משנה says חכמים already released them. רב יוסף gives another version of רב אסי's words: a חכם may release only vows that are like these four. From this the גמרא learns that רב אסי holds אין פותחין בחרטה, so regret alone is not enough to release a vow. Then the גמרא tells stories of רב הונא and רבה בר רב הונא, who released vows using two different questions. A ברייתא shows that these same two questions come from רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי. After a memory aid, more stories follow about how רבי אסי, רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן opened vows. רבי יוחנן's story, about a mother who vowed concerning her daughter, continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: The cold-water case is not like the bargaining case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from the צונן case. There it is clear the person meant more than he said. In the bargaining case we cannot tell what he meant.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are the cases really the same? With cold water, righteous people say little and do much, so 'cold water' clearly meant a whole meal. Here it is unclear. Maybe the seller really means he will accept less than a סלע and the buyer will pay more than a שקל, so it is just bargaining talk (זירוזין). Or maybe he means exactly what he said, and it is a real vow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the attempt to answer the bargaining question from the cold-water case in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the cold-water case everyone knows that 'have some cold water' is a polite way of inviting someone to a full meal, so the vow was clearly about the meal. A bargaining vow could go either way. The seller may be pushing for a good price, or he may truly refuse to go lower. Because the two cases are different, the proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Are they comparable? A way of rejecting a comparison
Cold water, from the case in the משנה
A doubt, something uncertain
Urging or pressuring words, like bargaining talk, not a true vow
Exactly, precisely as stated

steps.confusionAlert: 'Little' and 'much' here do not describe the vow itself. They describe the host's invitation: he says 'cold water' but means a full meal. That is why the vow is understood as being about the meal.

phrases.english: Are they comparable?
Regarding the cold water case,
the righteous say little and do much —
but here it is uncertain:

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְמָא פָּחוֹת מִסֶּלַע וְיוֹתֵר עַל שֶׁקֶל קָאָמַר,
phrases.english: perhaps he really means less than a sela and more than a shekel,
and it is just urging,
or perhaps he means exactly what he says,
and it is a real vow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought just before this section, from the cold-water case in the משנה, for the bargaining-vow question.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof completely. The cold-water case cannot teach us about bargaining vows.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In the cold-water case the speaker clearly meant something bigger. In bargaining, what the speaker meant is truly unclear.

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא leaves the bargaining-vow question unanswered.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the proof was rejected and no other answer is found, the גמרא closes the topic with 'תבעי': the question remains open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source settles whether a bargaining vow counts as זירוזין or as a real vow. Leaving it as a doubt means later פוסקים will have to rule on it using the rules for a doubt in vows.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it remain a question. The question is left unanswered

steps.whatToRemember: A bargaining vow ('I won't sell for less than a סלע' / 'I won't pay more than a שקל') is left as an unresolved doubt. We cannot tell whether it is זירוזין or a real vow.

phrases.english: Let it remain unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the topic after the proof in step 1 was rejected.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether a bargaining vow counts as זירוזין is left as an open question.

steps.title: רב אסי: the four vows still need a חכם
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב אסי: the four vows listed in the משנה still need to be brought to a חכם to be released.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב אסי: these four vows need to be asked about before a חכם.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב אסי rules that the four vows in the משנה are not released by themselves; a חכם must release them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed four vows that חכמים released: זירוזין, הבאי, שגגות, and אונסין. One could read that as meaning they never take effect at all. רב אסי says that one still needs שאלה לחכם, a formal request to a חכם, to be released.

keyTerms.meaning: The four vows listed in the משנה: זירוזין, הבאי, שגגות, אונסין
Asking a חכם to release a vow

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב אַסִּי:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav Asi said:
these four vows
phrases.notes: These are the four from the משנה: urging vows, exaggeration vows, mistaken vows, and forced vows.

phrases.english: require a request to a sage.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic about the four released vows of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The four vows of the משנה still need a חכם's release.

steps.title: שמואל objects: the משנה says they are already released
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה reports that when he told this to שמואל, שמואל objected that the משנה says חכמים already released these vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה says: When I said this before שמואל, he said: The תנא teaches 'four vows חכמים released,' and you say they need a request to a חכם?!
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל challenges רב אסי's ruling using the plain wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says 'הִתִּירוּ חֲכָמִים': the חכמים have already released these vows. If they are already released, there is nothing left for a חכם to do. So שמואל holds that these vows never bind at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא teaches. Quoting the משנה's wording
The חכמים released them

phrases.english: When I said it before Shmuel,
phrases.notes: 'I' is רב יהודה, who passed on רב אסי's ruling.

phrases.english: he said: The tanna teaches
'The Sages released four vows,'
and you say they require a request to a sage?!

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אַמְרִיתָא קַמֵּיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל, אָמַר: תַּנָּא תָּנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב אסי's ruling from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's claim that the four vows need שאלה לחכם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's words 'הִתִּירוּ חֲכָמִים' mean the vows are already released, so a חכם is not needed.

steps.title: רב יוסף's version: a חכם may only release vows like these four
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף passed on רב אסי's teaching in a different form: a חכם may release only vows that are similar to the four vows of the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף taught this teaching in this wording: רב יהודה said in the name of רב אסי: a חכם may release only vows similar to these four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of רב אסי's statement. In this version רב אסי is not saying the four vows need a חכם, so שמואל's objection does not apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version the four vows are the model for what a חכם may release. A חכם may release a vow only when, like these four, it was never truly meant as a vow or was made by mistake. This limits what a חכם can do and fits with the משנה saying the four themselves are already released.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught it. Passed the teaching on
Version, wording
Similar to, of the same kind as
Allowed to release (a vow)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion that argues with step 3. It is another report of what רב אסי himself said.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef taught it,
this teaching, in this version:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב אַסִּי:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav Asi said:
A sage is not permitted to release
except vows similar to these four vows.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף מַתְנִי לַהּ לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא בְּהַאי לִישָּׁנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of רב אסי's ruling from step 3, one that avoids שמואל's objection in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חכם may release only vows that are like the four vows of the משנה.

steps.title: So רב אסי holds that regret alone is not enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that, in this version, רב אסי holds אין פותחין בחרטה: a חכם may not release a vow just because the person now regrets it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that we do not open a vow based on regret.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind רב יוסף's version of רב אסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a חכם can only release vows like the four, he needs a real reason the vow was flawed from the start. 'I'm sorry I vowed' (חרטה) is not enough. He must find a פתח: a fact that, had the person known it, would have stopped him from vowing.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds
Opening, finding grounds to release a vow
Regret

steps.whatToRemember: By רב יוסף's version, רב אסי limits a חכם to vows like the four in the משנה. This means a vow cannot be released based on חרטה (regret) alone.
steps.whyThisMatters: Whether פותחין בחרטה is a central question in the laws of releasing vows (התרת נדרים).

phrases.english: He holds that we do not open a vow based on regret.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion about רב אסי's view from the version in step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: By this version, רב אסי holds אין פותחין בחרטה.

steps.title: רב הונא releases a vow because the man no longer wants it
steps.stepSummary: A man came to רב הונא to release his vow. רב הונא asked if he still felt the same way. The man said no, and רב הונא released the vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man came before רב הונא. רב הונא asked him: 'Is your heart still set on this vow?' He said: 'No.' And רב הונא released the vow for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about רב הונא releasing a vow. This shows a view different from the one just given for רב אסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's only question was whether the man still felt the way he did when he vowed. Once the man said no, that was enough. So רב הונא releases a vow based on regret alone, which is פותחין בחרטה, the opposite of רב אסי's view from step 6.

keyTerms.meaning: Is your heart upon you? Do you still feel the way you did when you vowed?
And he released it for him
A חכם may release a vow because the person now regrets it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two views. רב אסי (step 6) holds that regret alone is NOT enough. רב הונא here released the vow based on regret alone.

phrases.english: There was a certain man who came before רב הונא,
He said to him: Is your heart upon you?
phrases.notes: He means: do you still feel the way you did when you made the vow?

phrases.english: He said to him: No. And he released it for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story showing the view opposite to רב אסי's: a vow may be released based on regret.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא releases a vow once the person says he no longer feels the way he did when he vowed.

steps.title: רבה בר רב הונא releases a vow with a different question
steps.stepSummary: A man came to רבה בר רב הונא. He asked: if ten people had calmed you down at that moment, would you have vowed? The man said no, and the vow was released.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man came before רבה בר רב הונא. He asked him: 'If there had been ten people to calm you down at that moment, would you have made the vow?' He said: 'No.' And he released the vow for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second story, this time about רבה בר רב הונא, who also released a vow. His question to the man was worded differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא asked about how the man feels now. רבה בר רב הונא asks about the moment of the vow: if people had calmed you down then, would you still have vowed? If the answer is no, the vow is released.

keyTerms.meaning: Who would have calmed you down
At that moment, when you made the vow
And he released it

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא דַּאֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא,
phrases.english: There was a certain man who came before רבה בר רב הונא,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִילּוּ הָיוּ עֲשָׂרָה בְּנֵי אָדָם
phrases.english: He said to him: If there had been ten people
who would have calmed you down at that moment,
would you have vowed?
He said to him: No. And he released it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא דַּאֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story, parallel to רב הונא's, using a different question to release the vow.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה בר רב הונא releases a vow if the person says he would not have vowed had others calmed him down at the time.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows both questions come from תנאים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records רבי יהודה using רב הונא's question and רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי, quoting his father, using רבה בר רב הונא's question.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי יהודה says: We ask the person, 'Is this feeling still upon you?' If he says no, we release him. רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי says in his father's name: We ask the person, 'If there had been ten people to calm you down at that moment, would you have vowed?' If he says no, we release him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא showing that the two questions from the stories were already used by earlier sages, the תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's question matches רב הונא's question ('Is your heart upon you?'). רבי יוסי's question, passed on by his son, matches רבה בר רב הונא's question word for word. So each אמורא was following an earlier opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
Is this feeling still upon you?
We release him from the vow
In the name of his father

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to ask the person: רבי יהודה and רב הונא ask 'Do you still feel this way now?' רבי יוסי and רבה בר רב הונא ask 'Would you have vowed if people had calmed you down then?' Either way, if he answers no, the vow is released.

phrases.english: It was taught: רבי יהודה says:

phrases.aramaic: אוֹמְרִים לוֹ לָאָדָם: לֵב זֶה עָלֶיךָ?
phrases.english: We say to the person: Is this heart upon you?
phrases.notes: Same idea as רב הונא's question: does he still feel the way he did when he vowed?

phrases.english: If he says no, we release him.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם אָבִיו:
phrases.english: רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוסי says in the name of his father:

phrases.aramaic: אוֹמְרִים לוֹ לָאָדָם: אִילּוּ הָיוּ עֲשָׂרָה בְּנֵי אָדָם
phrases.english: We say to the person: If there had been ten people
who would have calmed you down at that moment, would you have vowed?
If he says no, we release him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source from the תנאים for both questions used in the two stories.
steps.raayaObject: The two ways of asking that רב הונא and רבה בר רב הונא used to release vows
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with רבי יהודה and רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי in his father's name

steps.title: A memory aid for the next discussion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a memory aid listing the sages who appear next: אסי, אלעזר, יוחנן and ינאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Memory aid: אסי and אלעזר, יוחנן and ינאי.)
steps.whatsHappening: This is not part of the argument. It is a memory hook that sets up the next discussion by listing, in order, the sages who will be quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא sometimes gives a סימן to help learners remember the order of several short statements. Here it tells us that statements from אסי, אלעזר, יוחנן and ינאי are coming next.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid that lists the coming topics or names in order

phrases.english: (Memory aid: אסי and אלעזר, יוחנן and ינאי.)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the current section and prepares the next set of statements.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling. It only lists the order of the sages in the coming discussion.

steps.title: רבי אסי asks if the person regrets the vow now
steps.stepSummary: A man came to רבי אסי to release his נדר. רבי אסי asked if he regrets it now. The man answered in a way that showed he did, and רבי אסי released the vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man came to רבי אסי. רבי אסי asked him: Do you regret your vow now? The man said: No? (meaning, of course I do!) And רבי אסי released the vow.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first story from the memory aid in Step 10. It shows the question רבי אסי used to release a נדר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אסי's opening is simple: he asks whether the person feels regret right now. The man's answer shows that he does, and that is enough for רבי אסי to release the vow. This is the first of several different 'opening questions' the גמרא lines up side by side.

keyTerms.meaning: A certain person who came before (a sage)
Now
You regret
He released it (the vow) for him

phrases.english: A certain person who came before Rabbi Asi
He said to him: Do you have regret now?
He said to him: No?
phrases.notes: Read his answer as a question back: 'Do I not regret it?' He means that he certainly does.

phrases.english: And he released it for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First of the stories promised by the memory aid in Step 10 (אסי).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אסי released a vow after the person showed that he now regrets it.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר asks if the person really wanted to vow
steps.stepSummary: A man came to רבי אלעזר. רבי אלעזר asked whether he really wanted to make the נדר. The man said he only vowed because people made him angry, and רבי אלעזר released the vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man came to רבי אלעזר. רבי אלעזר asked: Did you really want to vow? The man said: If they had not made me angry, I would not have wanted anything. רבי אלעזר said: Let it be as you want, and the vow was released.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second story from the memory aid. It shows the question רבי אלעזר used to release a נדר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר does not ask about how the man feels now. He asks whether the man truly wanted the vow in the first place. Since the man vowed only out of anger, the vow did not reflect what he really wanted, so it is released.

keyTerms.meaning: Did you want to vow?
They anger me / made me angry
I would not have wanted anything
Let it be as you want

phrases.english: A certain person who came before Rabbi Elazar,
He said to him: Did you want to vow?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִילּוּ לָא מַרְגְּזִין לִי
phrases.english: He said to him: If they had not angered me,
I would not have wanted anything.
He said to him: Let it be as you want.
phrases.notes: In other words, since you never really wanted this vow, it is released.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second story from the memory aid (אלעזר), giving a different opening question than רבי אסי's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר released a vow because the person only made it out of anger and never truly wanted it.

steps.title: A mother vows about her daughter and comes to רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: A woman made a נדר about her daughter and came to רבי יוחנן to release it. רבי יוחנן begins to ask her what she would have done if she had known what her neighbors would say about her daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain woman made a vow about her daughter, so that the daughter could not benefit from her. She came to רבי יוחנן. He said to her: If you had known that your neighbors would say about your daughter:
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third story from the memory aid, about רבי יוחנן. The גמרא is setting up his question here; the neighbors' words and the end of the story come on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's opening points to something the woman did not think about when she vowed: how her neighbors would talk about her daughter. The question breaks off here in the middle, so we do not yet hear what the neighbors would say or how the story ends.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman
She made a vow regarding her daughter
If you had known
Your neighbors

phrases.english: A certain woman who made a vow regarding her daughter,
phrases.notes: She vowed that her daughter may not benefit from her.

phrases.english: came before Rabbi Yochanan.
He said to her: Had you known
that your neighbors would say about your daughter:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third story from the memory aid (יוחנן). It begins here and is completed on the next עמוד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן begins an opening based on what the neighbors would say about the daughter. The full question and the ruling continue afterward.
